q: The study of the economy as a whole is
e: Macroeconomics studies the whole economy.

q: Which of these is a factor of production?
e: Land, labour, capital and enterprise are the factors of production.

e: At equilibrium, quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

q: Demand is price elastic when the price elasticity of demand is
e: If elasticity is more than 1, quantity responds strongly to price changes.

q: The reward for labour is
e: Labour earns wages.

q: The reward for land is
e: Land earns rent.

q: The reward for capital is
e: Capital earns interest.

q: A market with only one seller is a

e: Oligopoly means a few sellers dominate the market.

e: GNP = GDP + net income from abroad.

q: Per capita income is
e: It is the average income per person.

q: The central bank acts as the
o: lender of last resort to banks
e: Commercial banks can borrow from the central bank when in difficulty.

q: A main function of commercial banks is
e: Banks take deposits and lend to customers.

q: A progressive tax is one where
o: the rate rises as income rises
the rate falls as income rises
tax is paid only on goods
e: Higher incomes pay a higher percentage.

q: Value Added Tax (VAT) is an example of an
e: VAT is charged on goods and services, so it is an indirect tax.

q: Deflation is
e: Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level.

q: A country's balance of payments records
o: its transactions with the rest of the world
e: It summarises all payments in and out of the country.

q: The balance of trade is the difference between
e: It compares the value of visible exports and imports.

q: Devaluation is
o: a rise in the value of a currency
a deliberate fall in the value of a currency against others
e: It is an official lowering of a currency's exchange rate.

q: The law of diminishing returns states that
o: adding more of a variable factor eventually gives smaller extra output
all factors can be changed at once
e: Extra units of one input, with others fixed, eventually add less.

e: Rent does not change with the level of output.

e: Street lighting benefits everyone and no one can be excluded.

q: Division of labour means
o: each worker specialises in one task
e: Specialisation raises productivity.

q: A mixed economy has
e: A mixed economy combines private enterprise and government.

q: Optimum population is the population that gives
e: It is the size at which output per person is highest.

q: Cost-push inflation is caused mainly by
e: When production costs rise, firms raise prices.

q: A subsidy is
o: a payment by government to producers to lower costs
e: Subsidies reduce the cost of production or price to consumers.

e: PED = 20% ÷ 10% = 2, so demand is elastic.

e: Many sellers sell identical products and are price takers.

q: A profit-maximising firm produces the output at which
e: Profit is greatest where MC = MR.

e: Credit multiplier = 1 ÷ 0.20 = 5, so 5 × 1,000 = 5,000.

e: Buyers pay with bank deposits, which reduces banks' reserves and credit.

q: A budget deficit occurs when
e: A deficit means government spends more than it earns.

q: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established in
e: ECOWAS was formed by the Treaty of Lagos in 1975.

q: A major objective of OPEC is to
o: coordinate petroleum policies of member countries
e: OPEC coordinates oil output and pricing policies of its members.

q: The World Trade Organization (WTO) replaced the
e: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade became the WTO in 1995.

q: A country has a comparative advantage in a good when it
o: produces it with the most workers
produces it at a lower opportunity cost than others
e: Lower opportunity cost, not absolute output, defines comparative advantage.

e: Terms of trade = (120 ÷ 80) × 100 = 150.

o: use of rudimentary tools and land fragmentation
shortage of land in every region
e: Small, scattered farms and simple tools keep productivity low.

q: Crude oil's chief importance to the Nigerian economy is that it
o: employs most of the labour force
is the main source of foreign exchange earnings
is the largest tax on individuals
e: Oil exports earn most of Nigeria's foreign exchange and government revenue.

q: Economic development differs from economic growth in that development
o: includes improvements in living standards and welfare
e: Growth is a rise in output, while development also covers welfare and structural change.

q: A tax imposed on imported goods is called a
e: A tariff is a customs duty on imports.

q: A price ceiling set below the equilibrium price will lead to
o: a fall in demand to zero
e: At the lower price, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

q: The main disadvantage of a sole proprietorship is
e: The owner's personal assets can be used to pay business debts.

q: If a 5% rise in price leads to a 10% rise in quantity supplied, price elasticity of supply is
e: PES = 10% ÷ 5% = 2, so supply is elastic.

q: A firm's fixed cost is N2,000. At an output of 50 units, average fixed cost is
e: AFC = TFC ÷ output = 2,000 ÷ 50.

q: If nominal GDP is N1,200bn and the price index is 120 (base 100), real GDP is
e: Real GDP = nominal ÷ price index × 100 = 1,200 ÷ 120 × 100.

q: A rise in the price of a good leads to a movement along the supply curve. This is called
o: a shift of the demand curve
e: A price change moves along the curve; non-price factors shift it.
